NYCDOT is proposing a change to the City Map, land acquisition, and the implementation of Capital Project HWR00510, which is referred to in this Environmental Assessment Statement (EAS) as the Woodrow Road Connection at Veterans Road East. The proposed project is located in the Charleston and Sandy Ground/Woodrow neighborhoods of Staten Island and involves improvements to Woodrow Road between Bloomingdale Road on the east and Veterans Road East (the service road to the West Shore Expressway) on the west. The total length of the proposed project corridor is about 1,800 linear feet, of which about 280 linear feet west of Bloomingdale Road needs to be added to the City map. Assuming that the street mapping is approved, the proposed capital project calls for a comprehensive reconstruction of the entire proposed project corridor to NYCDOT street design standards, inclusive of new curbs and sidewalks, new paved surfaces and pavement markings, a raised and planted median and the necessary infrastructure (e.g., stormwater and sanitary sewers). To implement the proposed project, the City must acquire private land within the mapped Woodrow Road right-of-way; the land proposed to be acquired consists of portions of the front yards and driveways of 26 residential lots and vacant properties. With the proposed project, an estimated 120 street trees would need to be cleared. Therefore, DDC, in conjunction with the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation (DPR), would implement a tree replacement and protection plan as part of the project. Approximately 37,276 square feet of private property needs to be acquired to enable the proposed project, of which about 29,062 square feet is in the area of the proposed mapping and 8,214 square feet is within the mapped, but unbuilt, segment near the west project limit (at Veterans Road East). The proposed build year for the project (i.e., the year of completion) is 2018.

project_rows.project_description: The co-applicants, the New York City Educational Construction Fund (ECF) and 240 Nassau Street Holdings, LLC, are seeking a rezoning and other actions to facilitate the redevelopment of the project site (Block 110, Lot 25, and Block 111, Lot 1) with a mixed-use project including residential, retail, community center, and cultural space, public school facilities, and open space. The proposed project would result in the redevelopment of the project site with up to 1,502 mixed-income residential units (approximately 1,502,000 gross square feet [gsf]), 34,000 gsf of retail, and 45,000 gsf of community facility space. In addition, approximately 121,000 gsf of public school space would be developed to replace an existing outdated school with a modern facility and approximately 208 seats of additional school capacity would be provided with the proposed actions. The proposed actions would facilitate approximately 1,701,000 of gross floor area in four new buildings. The existing public school building was built in 1953. Due to its age, the schools electrical, ventilation, and acoustical systems are inadequate to serve the needs of the building. Additionally, nearly all of the schools classrooms and ancillary school space are in noncompliance with ADA accessibility standards. The proposed actions would provide state-of-the-art school facilities for pre-Kindergarten through 8th grade, achieve a better learning environment, and provide additional public school capacity in Community School District 13.    The proposed project will require several discretionary actions, including: (i) a zoning map amendment to change the project site from an R6 district to a C6-12 district; (ii) a zoning text amendment to modify Zoning Resolution (ZR) Section 74-752 to make the provisions applicable to the project site; (iii) a zoning text amendment to designate the project site as a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing (MIH) Area; and (iv) a special permit pursuant to ZR Section 74-75. In addition to the zoning approvals, the proposed project requires the transfer, reallocation, and lease of property among the developer, ECF, and the City of New York to allow for the schools in the new location, the proposed development, and ECF financing. Additionally, ECF would issue tax exempt bonds to facilitate construction of the school.

The proposed development would be a 7-story (85-foot tall at roof), approximately 105,900-gross-square-foot (gsf), residential building with 84 units of affordable housing, an approximately 3,900-gsf of performance space for use by local non-profits, approximately 3,000 gross square feet (gsf) of community facility space for administrative use and tenant and supportive services, and 30 parking spaces (the proposed project). The parking garage a would be located on the ground floor of the proposed building. The parking spaces would be reserved for New York City Department of Education (DOE) staff from the adjacent PS65 Mother Hale Academy public school, as replacement for the existing parking spaces used by DOE staff. There would be no parking for the new residential or community facility uses. The proposed project is expected to built and occupied in 2028, which is the project's anticipated build year. The proposed project would be Passive House-certified, and would include solar panels on the roof. The proposed project would be all-electric, relying solely on electricity for energy needs, including heating, cooling, and hot water. The proposed design of the new building would minimize air leakage, reduce heat transfer, and control moisture, all of which contribute to improved energy efficiency. The project site is City-owned (under DOE jurisdiction). The portion of Lot 1 (Tentative Lot 10) that would be occupied with the proposed project has an area of approximately 17,000 square feet; the remaining portion of Lot 1 is occupied with the existing PS 65 Mother Hale Academy and a schoolyard. In addition to the disposition, the proposed project would be facilitated by an Article XI tax exemption and construction funding from HPD through its Extremely Low and Low Income Affordability Program (ELLA) as well as a New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) Building of Excellence Grant. Absent the requested approvals, the project site would remain in its existing condition - a vacant area that serves as parking for DOE staff vehicles.
